author: JeffGold
quote: Rockstar said the romance story was optional and then tied the entire story to the romance and locked core basic features behind mandatory story progression. You cannot even save a custom car until you complete TWENTY-SEVEN missions. If you save money and weapons before a certain story point, all your progress will be wiped and reset when you reach that point. Are we really doing the "take the player's guns and gear" BS in 2026, Rockstar? Not being able to commit violence in your neighborhood makes no sense and is immersion-breaking, as are so many other issues in this game. Rockstar promised the most immersive and realistic game of all time, and yeah, it looks pretty, but it's missing so many basic features that have been in previous GTA sandboxes—it's hard to comprehend. For example, you can only take 32 pictures with the in-game camera, and the powerful in-game photo editor isn't viewable inside the game. Rockstar decided to turn the open world into a Bethesda-style loot operation, with houses and businesses serving as "dungeons," and the entire world doesn't even feel like GTA; it feels like something from the millennial quirky Marvel Cinematic Universe mixed with Gearbox-style humor. Why is there supernatural and sci-fi stuff in this game that is played deadly seriously? In every other GTA game, none of that was treated as real; it was a device used to mock conspiracy theorists and UFOlogists. Now, apparently, Rockstar has decided that GTA lore officially includes giant hulks, Bigfoots, and driving dogs. So much for realism, right, Rockstar? Totally immersion-breaking and ridiculous. The game constantly punishes you for playing how you want to play and restricts what you can and cannot do. It isn't an actual sandbox game; it's an artificial world with scripted events like a Ubisoft or Bethesda game. This is not a "next-gen" game. It's just more of the same we've already seen in a hundred other open-world games from this console generation. I have encountered numerous game-breaking bugs where objects randomly start pulling me into them, clipping through the cells and then randomly launching me across the map. At times, the game dropped to a legitimate 10–15 FPS on PS5 Pro when I had a five-star wanted level and a lot of action on screen. A totally unoptimized mess. The driving is terrible; it's way too easy; no vehicles have unique physics; everything is floaty and feels like driving on ice, and you can make sharp turns easily. The crashes are highly inconsistent and the damage to health makes no sense; you can be driving 150 mph on a bike and get launched 100 feet into a tree and barely take any damage. Realism, Rockstar? Immersion? The gunplay and combat improvements are completely undermined by the game being so easy that a baby could play it. You and all the enemies are bullet sponges; you can run around like a combination of John Wick and John Rambo and have no fear whatsoever of dying. You have to be a complete idiot to die and be doing so intentionally. The game has unfailable QTEs; literally all that happens is a slightly different cutscene with a few words of dialogue changed to no effect. The game has no ending; you literally just get thrown back to before the last mission, so none of your choices matter at all. You pretty much can't even beat the game. Rockstar just acts like you never did, no matter what you choose. That's the worst condemnation I can make of Rockstar. Even they couldn't commit to forcing the player to accept the consequences they spent so much time trying to build the illusion of. Completely unacceptable. There is so much wrong with this game; it's hard to even list it all. Is it all bad and a 0/10? No. But it's closer to that than a 10/10, that's for sure. Jason and Lucia are utterly annoying. Jason is a mumbling, marble-mouthed Wonderbread cornball doofus; Lucia is annoying, unlikeable ghetto trash with no positive characteristics, just a completely unsympathetic character you're supposed to like for some reason. This entire game is played deadly seriously, and it is one of the strangest tone clashes and decisions for a GTA game. But this is barely even a GTA game; it's a game wearing the skinsuit **** game. Simply put, this is not for Rockstar or GTA fans. It's for the modern gamer. Triple-AAA gaming is utterly obsessed with making "cinematic" and "emotional" stories and pretending they are Hollywood. Just stop; it is bad, and you are cringe and talentless. You aren't David Lynch, you aren't David Cronenberg, and you are not Terrence Malick. And you aren't Errol Morris. Stop trying to write these terrible stories and force players to sit through hours of cutscenes to do simple bits of gameplay. The writing here is so far removed from GTA. GTA was meant to be a satire of American life, not a deadly serious romance story. Yes, it still retains some of the GTA charm and humor, but it's vastly reduced compared to previous games and constantly superseded.
